cards.text: Ezra tells this one himself, friend. He's a priest and a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, and Artaxerxes, king of Persia, sent him to Jerusalem (Ezra 7:6, 11-14). Now Ezra writes down the family heads who came with him from Babylon.

Then comes the list of family heads, including Hattush from the descendants of King DAVID, and most of them have a group of men registered with them. One family head brings 28 men, another brings 300, and Ezra writes it all down like the most serious sign-up sheet in history.
Ezra gathers everybody at the canal that flows to Ahava, and they camp there three days. Then he walks the camp and searches, like a trip leader doing a head count before the bus pulls out.

cards.question: Ezra searches the camp by the Ahava canal, and he finds no ___ there.

cards.text: So Ezra sends a team of leaders and teachers to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and the name Elnathan shows up THREE times on that team. Somebody yells "Elnathan!" and three heads turn around.

cards.question: Ezra's team carries a message to Iddo and his kinsmen at Casiphia. True or false: the message asks them to bring ministers for the house of God.

cards.text: And then it happens, friend. LEVITES are brought to Ezra and his people.

cards.question: Levites are brought to Ezra and his people. What does Ezra say is behind it?
Sherebiah, a man of insight, is the first Levite named. True or false: Sherebiah makes the trip alone.
Also brought to Ezra are 220 ___ servants, all designated by name. David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites.

cards.text: Now they've got their Levites, and the road to Jerusalem is waiting. But Ezra stops everything right there by the Ahava Canal.

cards.question: Ezra wants them to humble themselves before God and ask for a safe journey for their children and all their possessions. So what does he proclaim?

cards.text: Here's the thing. There are enemies on that road, and the easy move is to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen, but Ezra's too ashamed to ask.

cards.question: Why is Ezra ashamed to ask King Artaxerxes for an escort of soldiers?

answers.text: He had told the king his God is gracious to all who seek Him
The king had already turned down his other requests
He knew the king needed every soldier to guard Babylon

cards.text: Think about it. Telling the king his God's got them and then asking for soldiers is like telling your boss "I got this" and then begging him to do it for you. So instead, they fast and petition their God about it.

cards.question: Ezra and the exiles fast and ask God for a safe journey. True or false: God grants their request.

cards.text: Next, Ezra sets apart twelve of the leading priests, plus Sherebiah, Hashabiah, a Levite from the descendants of Merari, and ten of their brothers. When a man picks TWENTY-FOUR people for one job, friend, that job is HEAVY.

cards.question: What does Ezra weigh out into the hands of these priests and Levites?

answers.text: Silver and gold and sacred articles
Spears and shields for the road
Grain and oil for the altar

cards.text: We're talking 650 talents of silver, 100 talents of gold, 20 gold bowls, and two articles of fine polished bronze as precious as gold. I lose my oven timer twice a day, friend, and NOBODY is ever handing me 100 talents of gold.
Then Ezra looks at the priests and Levites and tells them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy." That's not a pep talk, friend, that's a whole job description.

cards.question: True or false: Ezra says the silver and gold is tax money owed to the king.
Ezra gives the priests and Levites a job until the treasure is weighed out in Jerusalem. What is it?

cards.text: So the priests and Levites take charge of it all, and on the twelfth day of the first month they set out from the Ahava Canal. No soldiers, no horsemen, just families heading for Jerusalem with a FORTUNE in silver and gold.

cards.question: Ezra's group heads for Jerusalem with no escort. True or false: bandits steal part of the silver along the way.

cards.text: They make it all the way to Jerusalem and rest there three days. After a trip like that, friend, they EARNED it.

cards.question: On the fourth day, Ezra's group weighs out the silver and gold and sacred articles. Where do they do it?

cards.text: They weigh it all into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest, with Eleazar son of Phinehas (not the Eleazar who was Aaron's son) and two Levites right there with him. Four men waiting on one delivery, and NOBODY is rushing this handoff.

cards.question: Everything is verified by number and ___, and the total is written down right then.

cards.text: Then the exiles who came back from captivity sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel, including 96 rams and 77 lambs. These folks did NOT come all that way to sightsee, friend.

cards.question: Part of the offering is ___ bulls for all Israel.
True or false: Along with the rams and lambs, the exiles bring a sin offering of 12 male goats.

cards.text: They also hand the king's edicts to the royal satraps and governors west of the Euphrates. Hundreds of talents of silver and gold made it safe, and the last thing on the to-do list is still PAPERWORK.

cards.question: Once the satraps and governors get King Artaxerxes's edicts, what do they do?

answers.text: Assist the people and the house of God
Demand tribute from the priests and Levites
Send Ezra and his group back to Babylon

cards.text: Hold that thought, friend. Ezra just got to Jerusalem, and this story isn't finished with him yet.
